pageSubtitle: What is scheduled, how hard it usually hits, and what this market actually did last time
how1: The stars are the source's own impact rating — how violently a release usually moves markets. Three stars is not a buy or a sell, it is a warning that the next few minutes will be noisy.
how2: Only releases from currencies that actually drive this market are shown. Gold and crypto are priced in dollars, so US data matters to them even though neither is a currency pair.
how3: "Beat" and "missed" compare the released number to the forecast, and they are judged for the currency: fewer jobless claims than expected is a beat even though the number went down.
how4: Open "see past reactions" to measure what this market did in the 30 minutes after each past release. That is history, not a prediction — and if there are too few releases to measure, the panel says so instead of guessing.
title: Economic calendar
subtitle: Scheduled releases that can move {{symbol}}
empty: No scheduled release for these currencies in this window.
failed: The calendar could not be loaded. Price analysis is unaffected.
demoNote: These releases and numbers are synthetic. They are here so the screen works offline — never trade them.
noSource: No calendar source answered, so there is nothing to show. This is not the same as 'no news today'.
impactHint: The source's own 1–3 rating of how strongly a release usually moves markets. It is not our score and it says nothing about direction.
surpriseHint: Better or worse for the currency, not just higher or lower. A smaller jobless-claims number is a beat.

risk.blackout: {{title}} is {{time}} away. Spreads widen, stops get hunted and price can travel both ways before it picks one. Do not open a new position into this — wait for the release to settle.
risk.cautionHigh: A high-impact release ({{title}}) is {{time}} away. Either be in position already with your stop placed, or wait it out. Entering 10 minutes before a print is a coin flip, not a setup.
risk.cautionMedium: {{title}} is {{time}} away. Medium impact, so it is usually tradeable, but expect a quick spike at the release.
risk.clear: No scheduled release close enough to distort this market right now.
risk.noData: The calendar could not be read, so news risk is unknown. Treat it as unverified rather than clear — check your own calendar before entering.

riskHint: This answers whether a scheduled release is about to distort the market. It never says which way price will go. A blackout is a reason to wait, not a direction.
blackoutWindow: Blackout is {{before}} minutes before a high-impact release through {{after}} minutes after it.

reaction.title: What this market did last time
reaction.unavailable: This source has no release history for this event, so there is nothing to measure.
reaction.notEnough: Only {{count}} past releases could be measured. That is too few to generalise from, so no tendency is claimed.
reaction.window: Measured over the {{minutes}} minutes after each release, starting from the close of the candle before it.
reaction.betterGroup: When the number beat its forecast
reaction.worseGroup: When the number missed its forecast
reaction.tendencyMixed: No reliable direction: {{up}} up, {{down}} down. This release moves the market without telling you which way, so trade the reaction and not the forecast.
reaction.tendencyUnknown: Not enough measurable releases in this group.
reaction.skipped: {{count}} past releases were left out: they printed in line with the forecast, or we have no price data for that moment.
reaction.known: {{count}} releases on record at the source
reaction.fact: Over the last {{count}} measurable releases, the median move in the {{minutes}} minutes after this event was {{median}}.
reaction.interpretation: A release of this event has moved {{symbol}} by roughly that much before, so a stop sitting inside that distance is likely to be hit by the release itself rather than by your idea being wrong.
reaction.assumption: That the market reacts to this release the way it has recently. Regime changes, positioning and whatever else is happening that day can make the next one look nothing like these.
reaction.disclaimer: This is a measurement of past releases, not a forecast. Nobody knows the next number, and the same number can produce the opposite move depending on what the market already expected.
